newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: POLL - S.Africa to show healthy June trade balance.
newsitem.headline: POLL - S.Africa to show healthy June trade balance.

text.p: South Africa's trade balance is expected to have continued well in the black in June, underpinning hopes for an improvement in the current account over the second quarter.
The Customs and Excise department is expected to release the data in the latter half of next week.
Economists polled by Reuters on average forecast a surplus of 1.28 billion for June from a 1.75 billion surplus in May. Estimates ranged between 800 million rand 1.8 billion rand.
Most economists said diamond exports would have a large bearing on the size of the surplus. Botswana diamond sales underpinned May's larger-than-expected surplus.
The trade data is notoriously volatile, in part due to the inclusion of trade statistics from Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland.
SMK Securities economist Herman van Papendorp said he expected a 1.8 billion rand surplus which, with a likely 1.5 billion services deficit, would give a current account surplus of 300 million.
He said exports were likely to have been boosted ahead of the phasing out of the General Export Incentive Scheme (GEIS) on July 11, which was likely to lead to a lull in July and August exports.
"If one looks a couple of months down the line I think the numbers won't look as healthy due to GEIS being removed as well as the fall in the gold price.
"Later in the year we should see heavy surpluses again," van Papendorp added.
EW Balderson economist Mike Schussler expected a one billion visible trade surplus but said the removal of GEIS would have a small impact.
"I think it will have a slight effect. But at the end of the day the amounts involved and the categories involved have been narrowed down considerably.
"It probably won't represent more than three to four percent of the surplus," he said.
Economists were mixed as to when gold's recent meltdown would begin to effect the trade balance.
"It all depends on the amount and timing of forward sales. It could be six months or so before we see any large impact," said one.
South Africa is expected to record a 1.4 billion rand deficit on the June quarter current account, according to a Reuters survey of economists in late June, after a 1.9 billion in the March quarter.
